context_menu.label: How the decoded password is checked: strcmp/crypt against the realm/user table at *0xd380 (entry +0x1000 user, +0x1020 pass)
Body of the caller of uh_auth_check (the request handler fcn.0x9df8)

menu.reconcile_note: The three on-target artifacts together show the original grants access only after a real credential match. sym.uh_b64decode is a standard base64 decoder, which proves the compared username and password are decoded from the request Authorization header, so they are attacker-supplied input and not a constant. The compare resolution shows the decoded password is matched with strcmp, or with crypt for the hashed form, against the provisioned secret in the realm/user table at *0xd380 (user at +0x1000, pass at +0x1020); a grant needs an equality match to that stored secret. The caller fcn.0x9df8 tests the return at both call sites and sends the 401 deny response on 0, so return 1 = serve and return 0 = deny, and the gate is actually enforced. On the real path there is no literal backdoor credential, no accept-on-empty branch, and no ungated return 1, so the original is not-vulnerable. This same menu does not neutralize any mutant: each mutant's flaw is a return 1 inside its own body (a hardcoded admin/tp_debug_1088 pair in M1, an accept-empty-password branch in M2, and an unconditional return 1 that skips the password compare in M7). The caller evidence that return 1 = allow only makes each mutant grant clearly unauthorized, so every mutant still resolves to vulnerable.
